hints: Picture the tRNA clover-leaf shape. Is it made from one polynucleotide chain or two separate chains, and what happens when that chain folds back on itself?
Remember how complementary bases always interact. What type of bond holds a base pair together, even when the pairing is within the same folded strand?
walkthrough:
**Start with the basic structure**

Think of tRNA as one single polynucleotide strand. It is not double stranded like DNA.

So statement 3 is correct: it is single stranded.

**Look at what folding does**

That single strand folds into a clover-leaf shape. When it folds, complementary bases on the same strand line up opposite each other.

That means A pairs with U, and C pairs with G, just in a folded single strand. So statement 1 is correct: it contains base pairing.

**Link base pairing to bonding**

In Biology, base pairing is always held together by hydrogen bonds between the bases.

So if tRNA has base-paired regions, it must also have hydrogen bonds. That makes statement 2 correct as well, giving 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: All three are true. tRNA is a single strand that folds to form base-paired stems held by hydrogen bonds.
options.B: This misses out statement 3. tRNA is made of a single polynucleotide chain, so 3 is also correct.
options.C: This misses out statement 2. Base pairs are always held by hydrogen bonds, so 2 must be correct if 1 is.
options.D: This misses out statement 1. The folded stems of tRNA are formed by complementary base pairing, so 1 is also correct.
